hint: Every member evolves from the same Pokémon.
explanation: Vaporeon, Jolteon, Flareon, and Espeon all evolve directly from Eevee.
definition: Species that evolve directly from Eevee.

hint: Think about how these Pokémon are obtained.
explanation: Omanyte, Kabuto, Aerodactyl, and Cranidos are obtained by restoring their corresponding fossils.
definition: Pokémon obtained by restoring or reviving their corresponding fossils.
boundary: Direct restored species, not every descendant.

hint: These Pokémon sit before a familiar evolution.
explanation: Pichu, Cleffa, Igglybuff, and Togepi are officially classified as baby Pokémon at the start of their evolution families.
definition: Species whose structured species record has is_baby true.
boundary: Classification represented as a species flag.

hint: Their classification comes from another dimension.
explanation: Nihilego, Buzzwole, Pheromosa, and Xurkitree are all classified as Ultra Beasts.
definition: Pokémon classified in the games as Ultra Beasts.

hint: They are the last stage of the same starter type.
explanation: Charizard, Typhlosion, Blaziken, and Infernape are fully evolved Fire-type starter partners.
definition: Final evolutionary forms of Fire-type first-partner families.
boundary: Final evolutionary stage of the Fire partner line.

hint: Each has the same dual typing.
explanation: Quagsire, Swampert, Whiscash, and Gastrodon all have the exact Water/Ground type combination.
definition: Default forms with both Water and Ground types.

hint: Look at powerful late-game evolution families.
explanation: Dragonite, Salamence, Garchomp, and Hydreigon are Dragon-type final evolutions commonly classified as pseudo-legendary Pokémon.
definition: Dragon-type final evolutions in the fan/community pseudo-legendary convention.
boundary: Community convention, not an official Pokédex flag.

explanation: Mew, Celebi, Jirachi, and Manaphy are all Mythical Pokémon rather than ordinary legendary or high-stat species.
definition: Species whose structured species record has is_mythical true.
boundary: Mythical, not the broader Legendary label.

hint: They share a type and debut region.
explanation: Arbok, Nidoqueen, Muk, and Weezing are Poison-type Pokémon introduced in Kanto's first generation.
definition: Generation I species whose default forms include Poison.
boundary: Kanto means debut generation and region, not current habitat.

hint: Their original evolution method required another player.
explanation: Alakazam, Machamp, Golem, and Gengar originally evolved only when their previous stages were traded.
definition: Species reached by the original no-item trade trigger.
boundary: Original method; later alternate methods are excluded.

hint: On debut, none evolved from or into another Pokémon.
explanation: Tauros, Kangaskhan, Snorlax, and Miltank were single-stage Normal-type Pokémon when each debuted.
definition: Normal-type species introduced without an evolution relative at debut.
boundary: Only at debut; later family additions do not rewrite the historical condition.

hint: An item triggers the final evolution.
explanation: Arcanine, Vileplume, Starmie, and Chandelure evolve from their previous stages when an evolution stone is used.
definition: Species reached from their previous stages with an evolution-item trigger.
boundary: Original stone method; Vileplume intentionally overlaps Kanto Poison.
